question.problem: Given that $X∼\text{Bernoulli}(0.9)$ and $Y∼\text{Bernoulli}(0.4)$ are independent, calculate $P(X=1\,\cap \,Y=1).$
question.worked_solution:
Using the multiplication law for independent events, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X=1\,\cap \,Y=1) & =P(X=1)\cdot P(Y=1).\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since $X∼\text{Bernoulli}(0.9),$ we have

$$
P(X=1)=0.9,\,P(X=0)=0.1,
$$

and since $Y∼\text{Bernoulli}(0.4),$ we have

$$
P(Y=1)=0.4,\,P(Y=0)=0.6.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X=1\,\cap \,Y=1) & =P(X=1)\cdot P(Y=1) \\  & =0.9\cdot 0.4 \\  & =0.36.\end{aligned}
$$
